text: Attempt 15: the proven layout of attempts 11-14 with every home zone DENSE (people per tile has been 17-20 in every big attempt; dense reached 26-31 in attempts 7-8). Taxes 6%, factories at most 7%.

Attempt 14 ended at 23,580: healthy but slow, nine loans. All fourteen attempts hit the same money wall at about $3 per person; attempt 15 tests the one big lever left untried at scale: dense homes from day one.
Loan #3 ($10,000): the second coal plant had not fitted the cash after the dense blocks (dense zoning costs $10/tile); 109 buildings went dark.
play.sh now lists every stop reason (it had shown only the land alarm when power was also out).
East block (half shops, dense homes, $3,147), east road link ($1,060), west factory strip (factory and shop demand at max).
Rezoned 68 empty dense home tiles (east block x118-121 y38-54) to shops ($352): 390 empty home tiles, home demand -1,376, unemployment 16%, shop land short.

Feb 2005: 10,900 people. Dense homes filled faster than jobs: home demand fell to -2,000 with 390 empty home tiles and unemployment rose to 16%. So density works for people per tile; the constraint moves to jobs.
Second seaport (20 tiles, $3,162) next to the first: factory stall with 74 empty tiles. District 6 (dense homes + shops, $3,704) and its water joint to the main.
Plan slip: district 5 was never built in this attempt while later plans assumed it (district 6's water came through it). Audit flagged the dry district; joined it to the main directly.

Attempt 15 ends Jul 2011 at 18,260 (peak). Dense homes reached 26.8 people per tile (vs ~18), but the city stopped at the same ~18,000: factories stalled with empty land even after a second seaport, unemployment 13-14%.
